episodes.title: Informal Trade Behind Wiregrass Restoration
episodes.blurb: Interviews with 20 Florida landowners, land managers, and conservation staff show wiregrass restoration runs on trust-based swaps of seed, burn crews, and equipment. Seed costs about $1,700 per pound, and goodwill, more than profit, drives the sharing.

citation.title: The informal economy of wiregrass production for longleaf pine restoration in Florida

episodes.feed_title: Carney et al. 2024 Informal Trade Behind Wiregrass Restoration. Trees, Forests and People

episodes.title: Late Season Caribbean Hurricanes
episodes.blurb: Covers the October–November 2020 Atlantic hurricane finish, with five major hurricanes driven by low wind shear and warm western Caribbean water. A simple summer model using the ENSO longitude index and Atlantic warm pool would have predicted the surge.

citation.title: A Hyperactive End to the Atlantic Hurricane Season October–November 2020
citation.journal: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society

episodes.feed_title: Klotzbach et al. 2022 Late Season Caribbean Hurricanes. Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc.

episodes.title: Cyclone Winds and Forest Recovery
episodes.blurb: Twenty years of MODIS greenness data from southwest Pacific island forests show minor damage below about 50 meters per second, rising damage above that, and a sharp jump above about 75, with wide scatter.

citation.title: Tropical Cyclone Impact and Forest Resilience in the Southwestern Pacific

episodes.feed_title: Delaporte et al. 2022 Cyclone Winds and Forest Recovery. Remote Sensing

episodes.title: Wind Tracks Forest Growth
episodes.blurb: Wind measured above a Michigan mixed-deciduous forest tracked tree height growth in the leaf-off season, about twelve centimeters a year, matching tree censuses. Yet adding yearly canopy detail barely improved friction velocity models.

citation.title: Canopy-structure effects on surface roughness parameters: Observations in a Great Lakes mixed-deciduous forest

episodes.feed_title: Maurer et al. 2013 Wind Tracks Forest Growth. Agric. For. Meteorol.

episodes.title: Resistance Versus Resilience After Storms
episodes.blurb: A synthesis of more than 4,000 coastal monitoring time series from 26 tropical cyclones, mostly estuaries and offshore waters. Ecosystems that resist storm change tend to recover slowly, and those that change more recover faster.

citation.title: A general pattern of trade-offs between ecosystem resistance and resilience to tropical cyclones

episodes.feed_title: Patrick et al. 2022 Resistance Versus Resilience After Storms. Science Advances

episodes.title: Stoddard and the Case for Fire
episodes.feed_title: Way 2006 Herbert Stoddard and the Case for Fire in Longleaf. Environmental History
episodes.blurb: A historical essay on Herbert Stoddard in the Red Hills of Georgia and Florida. Way argues he helped launch wildlife management, legitimized fire in longleaf forests, and showed working farmland can hold diversity.

citation.title: Burned to be Wild: Herbert Stoddard and the Roots of Ecological Conservation in the Southern Longleaf Pine Forest

episodes.title: Heavy Rain and Acorn Crops
episodes.feed_title: Patterson et al. 2026 Heavy Summer Rain Days and Next-Year Oak Acorn Crops. Ecological Indicators
episodes.blurb: At Bent Creek Experimental Forest, the heaviest 10 percent of early-summer rain days tracked next year's chestnut and white oak acorn crops; light rain showed no link. For white oak they explained about three quarters of variation.

citation.title: Infrequent, high-volume rainfall events modulate acorn production for two common oak species in Western North Carolina, USA

episodes.title: Longleaf Pine on Delmarva
episodes.feed_title: Sheridan et al. 2026 Longleaf Pine Native to the Delmarva Peninsula. Sci Rep
episodes.blurb: Dead wood, DNA, radiocarbon dates and a remeasured herbarium specimen show longleaf pine once grew on the Delmarva Peninsula, outside the standard range map. Whether this northern stock was genetically distinct, or survives, remains unknown.

citation.title: DNA confirmation of morphologically identified pine remnants to verify the historic range of a keystone species in North America
